Company description:
We’ve been around for a long time. Since 1875 in fact.

We were founded by a businessman and MP called George Holloway, from Stroud in Gloucestershire.

He saw what happened when his employees got ill or had an accident, and how it impacted their lives. So, he did something about it and came up with an innovative and new type of insurance.

The idea was basically that everyone regularly paid a small amount into a pot of money. Then if someone was unlucky and became too unwell to work, they’d get paid some money back out of the pot as a replacement income.

Fast forward to today, and we’re still insuring people against becoming too unwell to work. 

We’re also still owned by our members. The only reason we exist is to help them, not make money for anyone else. Plus, we’re still based in sunny Gloucestershire!

Whilst we’ve been around a long time, we treat every day as an opportunity to keep improving, innovating and make a difference to our members lives.

- people involved in the adoption or protection of children
- businesses involved in commercial disputes
- individuals asserting their employment rights or challenging the decisions of government bodies

Bio:
After more than 17 years leading projects, programmes and business transformation initiatives, I’ve learned that strategy alone rarely creates alignment. Shared purpose does. 
	
Because no matter how strong the plan, roadmap or operating model is, people are usually trying to answer something much more personal:

- What does this mean for me?
- Where do I fit?
- Does my experience still matter?
- Can I see myself in the future being described?
		
That human side of transformation is what interests me most and I am particularly interested in the role storytelling, communication and leadership play in transformation. 

I’ve spent much of my career leading teams and delivering complex business change, and one thing I’ve seen over and over is:
		
The technical side of transformation is rarely the hardest part. Creating belief, clarity and alignment is.

Currently, I lead a team of Project Management professionals delivering business change and transformation initiatives at Pacific Life Re. My focus is on enabling successful delivery of change through strong leadership, stakeholder alignment, scalable PM capability and creating environments where teams can navigate complexity effectively.

Throughout my career, I’ve worked across:
- Process redesign
- Technology implementation
- Organisational change
- Operating models
- Global cross-functional delivery
		
I’m particularly passionate about storytelling in transformation and how communication, leadership and shared meaning influence whether change is simply implemented… or genuinely embraced.

Because in my experience, people don’t necessarily resist change. They resist stories or futures they can’t see themselves in.

We’ve been around for a long time. Since 1875 in fact.

We were founded by a businessman and MP called George Holloway, from Stroud in Gloucestershire.

He saw what happened when his employees got ill or had an accident, and how it impacted their lives. So, he did something about it and came up with an innovative and new type of insurance.

The idea was basically that everyone regularly paid a small amount into a pot of money. Then if someone was unlucky and became too unwell to work, they’d get paid some money back out of the pot as a replacement income.

Fast forward to today, and we’re still insuring people against becoming too unwell to work. 

We’re also still owned by our members. The only reason we exist is to help them, not make money for anyone else. Plus, we’re still based in sunny Gloucestershire!

He saw what happened when his employees got ill or had an accident, and how it impacted their lives. So, he did something about it and came up with an innovative and new type of insurance.

The idea was basically that everyone regularly paid a small amount into a pot of money. Then if someone was unlucky and became too unwell to work, they’d get paid some money back out of the pot as a replacement income.

Fast forward to today, and we’re still insuring people against becoming too unwell to work. 

We’re also still owned by our members. The only reason we exist is to help them, not make money for anyone else. Plus, we’re still based in sunny Gloucestershire!

Whilst we’ve been around a long time, we treat every day as an opportunity to keep improving, innovating and make a difference to our members lives.

Company description:
LV= is a protection, investment and retirement specialist and one of the UK’s leading life and pensions mutual insurers.

Our 1,300 people help our members and customers protect their income while they are working and maximise it when they stop. By doing this we enable people to live financially confident lives.

We offer a range of products, services and advice and serve over a million members and customers. They hold a variety of products with us including life insurance, income protection, investments and retirement income solutions such as equity release, fixed term annuities and drawdown products. We want members to be able to plan for a financially secure future. We put our members at the heart of all that we do.

We believe that everyone should have access to independent, regulated financial advice. It shouldn't be seen as a luxury for the few who can afford it or who are experienced in using it. Why? Because it provides financial and emotional benefits. Good advice ensures better financial outcomes and frees people from the worry of making complex decisions that could have long-term implications.

We work with a wide range of financial advisers and it is through them that the majority of customers will buy our products and services.

We also licence our brand to LV= General Insurance Group (LV= GI), a subsidiary of Allianz Holdings plc. LV= General Insurance is one of the largest personal insurers in the UK and looks after the car, home, landlord, pet and travel insurance needs of over 4.5 million customers.

Bio:
I am the Head of Sustainability Advocacy (UK and EU) at Aviva, having previously been the Head of Climate Policy at Aviva Investors. As part of my current role, I co-ordinate – and help develop - Aviva’s public policy advocacy positions relating to climate policy and broader topics of environmental sustainability in the UK and EU. As part of this, I work closely with investment teams and other business units across Aviva to help identify key areas of public policy change that can help unlock greater levels of private investment in low carbon infrastructure and businesses across different sectors of the economy. I regularly engage with public policy makers in the UK and EU on a wide range of climate, low carbon, and environmental sustainability policy topics. I also provide climate, low carbon and nature policy insights to investment, commercial and sustainability colleagues across the business. 

I am also currently a Trustee of not for profit think tank, the Institute of European Environmental Policy UK (IEEP UK).    

Prior to joining Aviva (2025) and Aviva Investors (2023), I was the executive director of the Aldersgate Group for 8.5 years, a membership organisation that drives policy change to build a net zero emissions, environmentally sustainable and competitive economy in the UK and the EU. During my tenure, the Aldersgate Group grew from around 25 to over 65 member organisations. This included business members from across the economy with a collective global turnover of around £600bn, as well as a wide range of civil society and academic organisation members. I oversaw the group's strategy, finances, public affairs and media work and supported a policy work programme covering the net zero transition in all key sectors of the economy, nature restoration, resource efficiency, green finance, low carbon skills and trade policy.

Prior to joining the Aldersgate Group, I spent 4 years as Head of Climate and Energy Policy at WWF UK, where I oversaw its policy programme on energy, transport, industry, emissions trading and took part in joint policy and campaign projects with WWF EU and WWF International. I spent the first 6 years of my career working as a commercial energy and environmental lawyer with City of London law firm CMS, where I advised a range of energy companies, financial institutions and regulators on electricity market reform, renewable energy projects, carbon capture and storage, oil and gas, emissions trading and climate legislation. 

Franco-British and proud father of 3 great kids.

We’ve been around for a long time. Since 1875 in fact.

We were founded by a businessman and MP called George Holloway, from Stroud in Gloucestershire.

He saw what happened when his employees got ill or had an accident, and how it impacted their lives. So, he did something about it and came up with an innovative and new type of insurance.

The idea was basically that everyone regularly paid a small amount into a pot of money. Then if someone was unlucky and became too unwell to work, they’d get paid some money back out of the pot as a replacement income.

We’re also still owned by our members. The only reason we exist is to help them, not make money for anyone else. Plus, we’re still based in sunny Gloucestershire!
